raw_text:
Great—here’s a structured 12-week program for a 31-year-old recreational lifter with PCOS, irregular cycles, HbA1c 5.8, BMI 28, clear medical clearance, and a goal of improving body composition and insulin sensitivity. Emphasis is on resistance training as the primary stimulus, controlled caloric intake to avoid under-fueling, and thoughtful recovery to support HPA axis health. No crash dieting or excessive cardio. The plan uses a weekly progression with periodized phases, built-in deloads, and notes on nutrition and recovery. Session timing assumes access to a full gym.

Assumptions and notes
- Training frequency: 4 days/week resistance-based, plus optional light active recovery if tolerated.
- Intensity: RPE-based progression (and load when possible). Focus on moderate volumes with progressive overload.
- Nutrition: Moderate caloric intake to support training and hormone balance. Emphasis on protein intake (~1.6–2.0 g/kg/day), balanced carbohydrates around training, and healthy fats. Given HbA1c 5.8 (prediabetes range), prioritize low-glycemic carbs around workouts and fiber-rich carbs otherwise. Consider periodic macronutrient titration based on progress.
- Sleep and recovery: Prioritize 7–9 hours sleep; include stress management and habit checks.
- Cycle considerations: Given irregular cycles, avoid interpreting cycle phase as a limitation; structure sessions consistently but consider hormonal symptoms on a weekly basis for potential autoregulation.
- Safety: Technique first. RPE adjustments if fatigue or soreness are high. Include optional regression moves for any exercise that causes discomfort.

Program overview
- Phases: Phase 1 (Weeks 1–3): Foundation and technique, establish routine, hypertrophy emphasis with moderate volume. Phase 2 (Weeks 4–7): Strength and endurance blend with progressive overload. Phase 3 (Weeks 8–12): Peak strength and body composition optimization with higher intensity and controlled deloads. Mini-deloads occur every 4th week or as needed.
- Weekly structure (example):
  - Day A: Lower body push/pull emphasis
  - Day B: Upper body push/pull emphasis
  - Day C: Lower body emphasis
  - Day D: Upper body emphasis
- Optional: 1–2 light cardio sessions per week (20–30 minutes, zone 2, optional, not excessive)

12-week plan with week-by-week structure

Phase 1: Foundation and technique (Weeks 1–3)
Goals: establish solid technique, build habit, begin hypertrophy emphasis, smooth RIR usage, begin insulin sensitivity benefits via resistance stimulus and protein intake.

Week 1 (Foundation)
- Session A (Lower body push/pull)
  - Squat pattern work: Goblet squat or bodyweight squat 2 sets x 10 reps (light), then Barbell back squat technique: 3 sets x 6–8 reps at RPE 6–7
  - Romanian deadlift (RDL): 3 x 8 reps at RPE 6–7
  - Leg press or split squats: 3 x 10
  - Glute bridge / hip thrust: 3 x 12
  - Core: anti-extension plank 3 x 30–45s
- Session B (Upper body push/pull)
  - Bench press or dumbbell press: 4 x 6–8 at RPE 6–7
  - Barbell row or Dumbbell row: 4 x 8–10
  - Overhead press: 3 x 8
  - Lat pulldown or assisted pull-up: 3 x 8–10
  - Accessory: lateral raises 3 x 12, triceps pushdown 3 x 12
- Session C (Lower body emphasis)
  - Front squat or goblet squat: 3 x 8–10
  - Deadlift variation (sumo or conventional): 4 x 6–8
  - Walking lunges: 3 x 12 steps per leg
  - Hip thrust: 3 x 10–12
  - Calf raises: 3 x 12–15
- Session D (Upper body emphasis)
  - Incline bench press: 4 x 8
  - Seated cable row: 4 x 10
  - Dumbbell flyes: 3 x 12
  - Push-ups or floor press: 3 x 8–12
  - Face pulls: 3 x 12–15
- Conditioning: Optional 1 zone-2 session for 20 minutes, if energy allows (not cranking cardio)
- Nutrition focus: Protein 1.6–2.0 g/kg/day; aim for ~25–35 g protein per meal. Balanced carbs around training (pre/post). Hydration.

Week 2 (Progression)
- Increase load modestly on compounds (2–5% if form solid) while maintaining reps.
- Maintain same exercise selection; adjust RPE targets to 6–7 for most sets, some sets at 7–8 if comfortable.
- Add a set to one accessory exercise per session to increase volume slightly.
- Recovery: 1–2 minutes between sets for big lifts; 45–60 seconds for accessory.

Week 3 (Technique consolidation and light overload)
- Dial in technique, add subtle progression:
  - Squat pattern: 4 x 6–8 at RPE 6–7
  - RDL: 3–4 x 8–10
  - Bench: 4 x 6–8
  - Barbell row: 4 x 6–8
  - Lat pulldown: 3 x 8–10
- Include 1 optional tempo cue for some sets (e.g., 3-second eccentric on squats), to improve control.
- Deload consideration: If fatigue or soreness high, shift Week 3 to deload: reduce intensity by 20–30% and keep volume 70%.

Phase 2: Strength and endurance blend (Weeks 4–7)
Goals: Build strength with lower reps, maintain hypertrophy. Improve insulin sensitivity via higher training density and more strategic timing of nutrition.

Week 4 (Load progression)
- Session A (Lower)
  - Back squat: 4 x 5 at RPE 7
  - RDL: 4 x 8
  - Bulgarian split squat: 3 x 8 per leg
  - Hip thrust: 3 x 8–10
- Session B (Upper)
  - Bench press: 4 x 5–6 at RPE 7
  - Barbell row: 4 x 6–8
  - Overhead press: 3 x 6–8
  - Pull-up/lat: 3 x 6–8
- Session C (Lower)
  - Deadlift variation: 3 x 4–5 at RPE 7
  - Front squat: 3 x 6–8
  - Lunges: 3 x 8 per leg
  - Calf raises: 3 x 12–15
- Session D (Upper)
  - Incline bench: 4 x 6–8
  - Seated cable row: 4 x 8–10
  - Dips or push-ups: 3 x 8–10
  - Face pulls: 3 x 12–15
- Conditioning: 1–2 light cardio sessions optional, keep low duration.

Week 5 (Volume and density)
- Similar structure but add a set to main lifts if technique solid:
  - Back squat: 4 x 6
  - Bench: 4 x 6
  - Deadlift: 3 x 5
  - Accessory volumes adjust to 3–4 sets
- Tempo: include controlled eccentric (3 seconds) for at least one set per main lift in the week.

Week 6 (Deload or light progression)
- If fatigue; deload: reduce all working sets by 20–30% and maintain movement quality.
- If energy allows: 5–10% load increase on main lifts; keep reps the same.

Week 7 (Rebuild intensity)
- Return to higher intensity with lower reps for main lifts:
  - Back squat: 4 x 4–5 at RPE 7–8
  - Bench: 4 x 4–5
  - Deadlift: 3 x 3–4
  - Rows and presses: 3–4 x 6–8
- Accessory emphasis: 2–3 sets of core and mobility work.

Phase 3: Peak strength and body composition optimization (Weeks 8–12)
Goals: Move toward higher intensity with conservative volume, maintain insulin sensitivity via disciplined nutrition and rest, finish with a perceptible body composition improvement.

Week 8 (Intense effort)
- Session A (Lower)
  - Back squat: 5 x 3–4 at RPE 8
  - Deadlift: 3 x 3–4 at RPE 8
  - Split squat: 3 x 8 per leg
- Session B (Upper)
  - Bench press: 5 x 3–4 at RPE 8
  - Barbell row: 4 x 6
  - Overhead press: 3 x 6
- Session C (Lower)
  - Front squat: 4 x 4 at RPE 8
  - Hip hinge accessory: 3 x 8
  - Calf raises: 3 x 12–15
- Session D (Upper)
  - Incline bench: 4 x 6
  - Horizontal pull: 4 x 8
  - Dips: 3 x 8–10
  - Face pulls: 3 x 12–15

Week 9 (Volume taper and technique)
- Slightly reduce load, keep technique crisp; focus on tempo and connection.
- Main lifts: 3–4 x 4–6 at RPE 7–8
- Accessories: maintain 2–3 sets of 8–12.

Week 10 (Repeat or rebuild)
- Return to higher rep ranges if needed for joints/soft tissue, e.g., 4 x 8–10 on accessory movements.
- Main lifts: 4 x 5–6 at RPE 7–8
- Conditioning: Up to 15–20 minutes zone 2 if energy allows.

Week 11 (Peak conditioning)
- Peak strength focus with minimal volume:
  - Back squat: 3–4 x 3–4 at RPE 8
  - Bench: 3–4 x 3–4
  - Deadlift: 2–3 x 3
  - Accessory: 2–3 x 6–8
- Mobility and recovery emphasis.

Week 12 (Testing and deload)
- Week 12 can serve as a testing/retrospective week or a light deload:
  - Optional 1RM estimates or rep max testing for main lifts, if appropriate and safe.
  - If not testing, perform 3–4 x 5–6 with light/moderate loads and finish with a full-body mobility sequence.
- Recovery plan: extended cool-down, focus on sleep quality, nutrition alignment, and stress management.

Training details and guidelines
- Sets and reps: Follow the week-by-week structure above, but keep within RPE 6–8. If the load is too heavy and form is compromised, reduce load and maintain reps.
- Progression rules: Aim for 2–5% load progression on main lifts each week when technique and recovery allow. If unable to increase weight, add one extra rep or an extra set on the accessory exercises.
- Exercise substitutions: If any exercise causes discomfort, swap with a biomechanically similar alternative (e.g., replace back squat with goblet squat or safety-bar squat; replace conventional deadlift with trap-bar deadlift or RDL if hip/back discomfort arises). Prioritize comfort and form over exact movement patterns.
- Accessory work: Keep 2–3 sets per accessory exercise; choose exercises that target abdominal strength, hip stability, glute engagement, and scapular health (e.g., carries, Pallof presses, bird dogs, face pulls).
- Warm-up: Begin each session with a 5–10 minute general warm-up (light cardio or dynamic mobility), followed by 5–10 minutes of activation and mobility tailored to the day’s lifts (glute activation, thoracic spine mobility, scapular rhythm).

Nutrition and recovery plan
- Daily protein target: 1.6–2.0 g/kg body weight. Distribute evenly across meals.
- Carbohydrate timing: Prioritize around workouts (pre-workout meal containing ~30–60 g carbs, post-workout meal with protein and carbs within 1–2 hours). Balance carbohydrates through the day with whole-food sources; monitor fiber intake (25–35 g/day).
- Fat: Ensure essential fats accompany meals; include sources like olive oil, avocado, nuts, and fatty fish. Do not severely restrict fats, as they are important for hormones and general health.
- Energy balance: Avoid extreme dieting. Aim for a slight caloric surplus or maintenance depending on goals. For insulin sensitivity improvement, a slight caloric balance with adequate protein and carbohydrates around training plus regular resistance training is typically beneficial.
- Hydration: 2.5–3.5 L/day baseline (adjust for body size and climate).
- Supplements: 
  - Vitamin D3 if deficient (per clinician guidance)
  - Omega-3 fatty acids (EPA/DHA) if dietary intake is low
  - Protein powder as convenient option to meet daily protein targets
  - Creatine monohydrate: 3–5 g/day can support strength and body composition; ensure hydration
- Vitamin/mineral considerations: Ensure iron status is adequate; PCOS clients may experience menstrual blood loss; consider iron check if fatigue persists. Selenium, zinc, and magnesium can support sleep and muscle function; discuss with clinician if considering high-dose supplementation.
- Meal timing strategy: 
  - Pre-workout: moderate carb + protein (e.g., Greek yogurt with fruit, or oats with protein)
  - Post-workout: protein + fast-absorbing carbs (e.g., whey protein shake with fruit or a balanced meal)
- Blood sugar awareness: Given HbA1c 5.8, monitor for signs of impaired glucose tolerance. Favor lower glycemic index carbs most of the day, with higher GI carbs around training for refill. If glucose patterns worsen, adjust diet and consider consult with endocrinologist or dietitian.

Recovery and lifestyle
- Sleep: Target 7–9 hours per night. Create a consistent sleep schedule.
- Stress management: Include 5–10 minutes of mindfulness, deep breathing, or light movement on rest days.
- Mobility and rehab: 10–15 minutes post-workout focusing on hips, thoracic spine, shoulders, and ankles. Include mobility drills to support technique and reduce injury risk.
- Deload strategy: Every 4th week, consider a deload week with 40–60% of normal intensity and volume to prevent overtraining and support HPA health.

Tracking and progression
- Track loads, reps, and RPE for each main lift weekly.
- Note symptoms: fatigue, sleep quality, mood, cycle irregularities, energy levels, and any menstrual symptoms.
- Adjust nutrition if the plan leads to noticeable energy deficits, consistent fatigue, or poor performance. Consider a nutrition check-in every 4 weeks.

Cycle considerations and PCOS specifics
- The plan uses resistance training as the primary stimulus; avoid long durations of high-volume cardio that could worsen energy balance.
- Emphasize consistent protein intake and recovery strategies to support insulin sensitivity and body composition changes.
- If cycle regularity shows improvement or worsens, you can adjust daily energy availability and training timing accordingly, but avoid major caloric restriction.

12-week timeline summary
- Weeks 1–3: Foundation and technique; emphasis on form and initial hypertrophy stimulus.
- Weeks 4–7: Strength and endurance blend; increased load and volume with progressive overload.
- Weeks 8–12: Peak strength and body composition optimization; higher intensity with controlled volume, with a plan for testing or deloading in Week 12.
